diagnostics.message:
[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.aws_lambda_function.syncer` should wait for `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.syncer_vpc_execution_role` when VPC execution is configured, so the role has the required VPC networking permissions before the function is provisioned for VPC use.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
When VPC subnets are configured, Lambda creation/operation requires the execution role's VPC networking permissions. The function currently depends on the role but not on the managed VPC execution policy attachment, so it may be created before those permissions are attached.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_lambda_function.syncer configures vpc_config from var.lambda_subnet_ids/var.lambda_security_group_ids, but has no dependency on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.syncer_vpc_execution_role, which attaches the AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole policy granting the ec2 networking permissions (CreateNetworkInterface, etc.) Lambda needs to attach ENIs. If the function is created before the attachment propagates, function creation fails or the function cannot reach the VPC ("Lambda was unable to configure your VPC"). Nothing else in the graph orders the attachment before the function, so an explicit depends_on is required.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_lambda_function.syncer configures vpc_config (via var.lambda_subnet_ids / var.lambda_security_group_ids), but it does not depend on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.syncer_vpc_execution_role, the resource that attaches AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole to its execution role. AWS creates the function's Hyperplane ENIs during function creation and requires the role to already have those EC2 network permissions; since the attachment and the function are currently only siblings under aws_iam_role.syncer_lambda, the function can be created before the policy is attached (and before IAM propagates it), causing "the provided execution role does not have permissions to call CreateNetworkInterface" failures. Add an explicit depends_on of the function on the attachment (a bare depends_on is appropriate here; the attachment is counted and has no attribute worth referencing).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
When var.lambda_subnet_ids is non-empty, aws_lambda_function.syncer is created with vpc_config, which requires the execution role to already have VPC networking permissions (AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole, attached by aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.syncer_vpc_execution_role). The lambda function only depends on the role itself and the var.lambda_subnet_ids variable, not on the attachment, so Terraform may create the function before the policy attachment is applied, causing CreateNetworkInterface permission failures or failed ENI provisioning. Follow the provider-documented pattern and add a depends_on from the lambda function to the VPC execution-role policy attachment.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.syncer` should depend on `:resource.aws_lambda_permission.syncer` so the EventBridge rule cannot become active with its target before invocation permission for EventBridge is installed. The target references the Lambda and rule, but not this permission.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The EventBridge target can be created before the Lambda invoke permission, leaving the rule unable to invoke the function until the permission is installed. Make the target wait for the permission.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The EventBridge target can be created before the Lambda invoke permission is installed, so scheduled invocations may be attempted without authorization. Make the target depend on the permission resource.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
aws_cloudwatch_event_target.syncer points the scheduled rule at aws_lambda_function.syncer, but the resource-based policy that grants events.amazonaws.com permission to invoke the function (aws_lambda_permission.syncer) is created independently. Until that permission exists, the rule's invocations are rejected. Add depends_on = [aws_lambda_permission.syncer] to aws_cloudwatch_event_target.syncer, mirroring the notification->permission ordering already used for the S3 trigger path (aws_s3_bucket_notification.on_deploy depends on aws_lambda_permission.on_deploy).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
aws_cloudwatch_event_target.syncer registers aws_lambda_function.syncer as the target of the EventBridge rule, but does not ensure that aws_lambda_permission.syncer (the events.amazonaws.com lambda:InvokeFunction permission) exists first. The AWS docs state that to have a Lambda invoked by an EventBridge rule you must set up the permission via aws_lambda_permission. The S3 path in this same module already handles the equivalent case with depends_on on aws_lambda_permission.on_deploy; the EventBridge target needs the analogous ordering to aws_lambda_permission.syncer.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
Uploading this trigger object can invoke the Lambda immediately, but the trigger object has no ordering dependency on the role's S3 access policy. Ensure the policy is attached before creating the trigger to avoid an invocation before the function has permission to access the distribution bucket.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The initial S3 object creation triggers the Lambda, but it can run before the role's S3 access policy is installed. Make the trigger wait for this policy so its first invocation can access the distribution bucket.
